prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S001: The mission of the Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system is to support continuous production of potable water that meets regulatory requirements, utility operating targets, and customer demand.
S002: The control system is intended to give operators timely visibility, dependable automatic control, and clear manual intervention points for the intake, treatment, laboratory, and distribution functions.
S003: The operational boundary begins at the River Intake Pump Station and Raw Water Screen Channel and extends through treatment, disinfection, finished-water storage control, and discharge to the High Service Pump Header.
S004: The River Intake Pump Station is known locally as Ironwood, but this document uses River Intake Pump Station as the canonical name.
S005: The River Intake Pump Station provides the first controlled pumping function and is operated to maintain reliable raw-water availability within approved withdrawal limits.
S006: The Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as part of the controlled intake process because debris loading, screen condition, and inlet restrictions directly affect downstream stability.
S007: Storm Intake Mode is an expected operating state used when river conditions require more conservative intake operation, closer operator review, or modified treatment readiness.
S008: The treatment scope includes the Coagulant Dosing Skid, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, Backwash Recovery Tank, and related instrumentation needed for routine control decisions.
S009: The Coagulant Dosing Skid supports chemical feed control based on approved setpoints, observed raw-water conditions, and operator direction.
S010: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are operated as parallel treatment assets with local equipment status, headloss indication, turbidity monitoring, and backwash control presented to plant staff.
S011: The Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller provide the principal control points for disinfection contact management and finished-water storage coordination.
S012: The SCADA Historian Server is known locally as Lantern, but this document uses SCADA Historian Server as the canonical name.
S013: The SCADA Historian Server stores operating data needed for trend review, compliance support, incident reconstruction, and performance evaluation.
S014: The control architecture assumes that programmable controllers, local panels, operator workstations, analytical instruments, and the SCADA Historian Server remain synchronized to plant time standards.
S015: Major external interfaces include electric power service, chemical delivery coordination, laboratory information handling, residuals removal scheduling, and distribution system communications.
